name: rendering-text
description: BitmapFont text rendering with revealable text component and prep/update systems
postInstallNotes:
## rendering-text installed

Text is driven by the `DynamicTextComponent` component (uses `BitmapFont` from MonoGame.Extended, which `rendering` pulls in transitively). For static labels, set `IsRevealed = true` and `VisibleCharacterCount = int.MaxValue` (see `LevelSelectionScreen.cs` for the canonical pattern).

Pipeline order:
- `TextUpdateSystem` (advances reveal state per-frame) BEFORE
- `TextPrepSystem` (writes glyph quads into `DrawComponent`) BEFORE
- `MasterRenderSystem`.

The reveal animation lives in this module today — `DynamicTextComponent` has `IsRevealed`, `RevealingSpeed`, `RevealStartTime`, and `VisibleCharacterCount` fields that `TextUpdateSystem` advances.

### Partial faces are loud now

A bitmap face renders a character it lacks as NOTHING ("São Paulo" → "So Paulo"). `TextPrepSystem` warns via `Logger` — once per face + character, never per frame — whenever it is about to drop one. Fold the content into what the face covers and register it once per face:

```csharp
var faces = new TextFacePolicyRegistry()
    .Register(monoCapsFont, new TextFacePolicy(
        TextFold.Chain(TextFold.Dashes, TextFold.Ellipsis, TextFold.Ordinals,
                       TextFold.StripDiacritics, TextFold.Upcase),
        silentDrop: true)); // dropping the rest is deliberate and tested

g.Add("textPrep", new TextPrepSystem(world, pixelPerfectRendering, faces));
```

Pass the SAME registry to every screen's `TextPrepSystem` (it carries the warn-once ledger). Query coverage directly with `GlyphCoverage.HasGlyph` / `Covers` / `MissingCodepoints`. Silent dropping is still available — as an explicit per-face opt-in.

**Premises:** `docs/premises.md`
